---
name: publish-game
description: "Publish, update or unpublish static HTML/JavaScript games on voyager.site, or upload builds to itch.io."
---

For voyager.site, use the built-in `voyager game` commands with the user's existing Voyager sign-in.
When publishing needs a Voyager sign-in, `voyager auth login --no-wait` opens it in the user's
browser; publish once they have signed in.

Use [browser games](../make-game/references/web.md)
for creation and preview tools. Bundle ESM, styles, fonts, images, audio and JSON locally;
use relative URLs (`./assets/...`, Vite `base: './'`). Hosting runs no backend code and gives
the game no privileged Voyager bridge.
Select the precise built folder containing `index.html`, such as `dist`. A selected single
HTML file is published as `index.html` and includes no siblings unless a thumbnail is named.
A PNG/JPEG/WebP thumbnail is optional for general publishing. If none is selected, tell the
user: **X will show a plain link card, not the playable game**. For an X game, follow
[playable X games](../make-game/references/x-player-card.md): its square poster with the title and "Tap to play" is
required. With a thumbnail, Studio supplies `twitter:card=player`, a player URL of the stable
root plus `?embed=1`, and a 480×480 frame.
Run `voyager game prepare --source-path ./dist --json`. For a thumbnail, also pass
`--thumbnail-path poster.png` (relative to the selected folder). Review **every included
path**, excluded paths, total bytes and returned `digest`. All included files become public.
Never put files or a folder
named `_v` at the bundle root: that exact namespace is reserved for hosted versions. Nested
`assets/_v/`, `_assets/` and `_v-game.js` are allowed.
For a first publication, pick a short readable slug for the game, such as `moon-hop`. Use
1–40 lowercase ASCII letters/digits with single hyphens between words; no leading/trailing
hyphen or `--`. The server adds the
random six-character suffix automatically; do not invent or choose it. After verifying that
the selected release matches the user's publishing intent, run
`voyager game publish --source-path ./dist --title "Moon hop" --slug moon-hop --digest REVIEW_DIGEST --confirm-public --json`,
replacing `REVIEW_DIGEST` with the exact value from prepare, and repeat the same thumbnail
option if used. The service rebuilds and compares the snapshot before uploading. If anything
changed, prepare/review again. `--slug` is optional and only
applies when the game is first created; omit it on updates. If it differs from an existing
game's slug, the service warns and keeps the permanent URL.
Return the confirmed public root URL, controls and validation performed. URLs have the form
`https://<slug>-<random6>.voyager.site`, for example `https://moon-hop-a2b3c4.voyager.site`.
The document itself is playable and carries
the title/thumbnail metadata; there is no separate landing page. For X releases, follow the Twitterbot tag, player/poster HTTPS 200,
and framing checks in [player-card checks](../make-game/references/x-player-card.md).

## Manage the same publication

To embed the game on a website, use its confirmed public root URL with `?embed=1`:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://ACTUAL_GAME_HOST.voyager.site/?embed=1"
  title="Game title"
  width="480"
  height="480"
  allow="autoplay; fullscreen"
></iframe>
```

- `voyager game status --source-path ./dist --json` reads authoritative state.
- Publish again from the same source path and account to update the same URL. When Voyager
  renames the chat folder, the publication follows it automatically. If a folder was moved,
  renamed or copied outside Voyager, status and publish return CONFLICT naming the game (title and
  URL) and its `--game-id`, and status may list `unlinked` games whose folders are gone. Ask the
  user whether this is that game: if so pass `--game-id ID` to keep its URL; only if they say it is
  a different game pass `--new-game` (it never updates an existing publication). Rename with
  `voyager game rename --source-path ./dist --title "New title" --json` without reuploading.
  Rename changes the displayed title only; the original slug and URL are permanent.
- `voyager game unpublish --source-path ./dist --confirm-unpublish --json` stops new public
  requests within 30 seconds, including old version paths.
- After a timeout, check status before retrying. A build folder that was deleted can still be renamed or unpublished through
  its original path.

Limits: 500 files, 10 MiB per file, 50 MiB unpacked, 30 MiB compressed ZIP. Supported assets and
path restrictions are reported by prepare.

Free accounts can have **two games live at once**. Updating an already live game preserves its
URL and uses the same slot. If the service reports HTTP 402 `free_game_limit`, explain it and let the
user choose which existing game to unpublish or offer [Voyager billing](https://voyager.so/dashboard/billing).

Free, Starter, and accounts without a plan receive a quick, permissive AI safety check before
activation. Plans above Starter skip content checks. Structural bundle validation applies to
every plan. If the AI check's rare content
refusal returns HTTP 422 `content_flagged`, show the service's reason verbatim and stop; do not automatically
retry, rewrite the game, or conceal content to pass. A model outage or
timeout does not block publishing; the check fails open.
A content refusal or failed upload leaves the previous live version unchanged.

Publication, updates and title changes can take up to 20 seconds to become visible at an edge
location. Unpublish
retains its 30-second maximum for stopping new requests.

Voyager hosts static games and blocks external network connections. Shared live rooms need the
user's own server and hosting that permits connections to it.

## itch.io

butler cannot create the game page. The user signs in with `butler login` in their own terminal (opens a browser).

`butler push <folder> user/game:<channel>` uploads a build; later pushes to the same channel upload only changes. Channel names containing `win` or `windows`, `linux`, `mac` or `osx`, or `android` set the platform tag. Add `--userversion 1.2.0` to label the version.

Browser builds need `index.html` at the folder root. After the first push, the user sets the page to HTML and marks the upload "played in the browser" on itch.io's Edit game page; butler cannot do this.
